messages:
adam_h: Hey all — pharmacy denied my refill for a specialty med (prescriber says its the maintenance therapy I need). They flagged "step therapy" and say I need a prior auth/exception. I paid out of pocket once but don't want to keep doing that. Anyone helped with a step therapy override?

adam_h: Details in case it helps:
```
Drug: Tensosumab 50mg/mL prefilled syringe
Prescriber: Dr. L. Stein (Rheum)
Dispense Date: 2026-04-10
Billed Amount: $1,220.00
Pharmacy denial code: STP-102 (step therapy)
```

tara_peopleops: Sorry you're dealing with that @adam_h. Which Redwood plan are you on? For many plans the process is: 1) provider submits prior auth, 2) if PA denied then file an exception/appeal with clinical rationale (provider letter), 3) finance/benefits can help with short-term advance or copay assistance while it processes.

ben_benefits: Agree. Practical tips: ask your prescriber to submit a PA using the carrier's specialty PA form and include chart notes showing prior failures or contraindications to step meds. If the drug is covered under the carrier's specialty pharmacy program, the specialty pharmacy can often escalate to medical review. Also check manufacturer PAP/copay card (can cover patient cost while appeal is in review).

prescription_support: I can help pull the carrier PA form and draft a one-page clinical justification template for Dr. Stein to sign. If you want, DM me the Rx date and I'll start the packet and contact the specialty pharmacy on your behalf.

pharmacy_bot: [automated] Carrier tips: For step therapy denials provide: 1) recent clinical notes, 2) lab results supporting need, 3) prior med trial documentation. Typical review time: 7-21 days for standard review; urgent (e.g., imminent harm) can be fast-tracked. Link: https://carrier.example/specialty-pa

adam_h: Thanks all. Please DM me the PA form and the template @prescription_support. I may ask Finance for a one-off reimbursement if I have to pay again this week. Appreciate the assist. :pray:
